research_context: Differences in intestinal flora between irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C) and functional constipation (FC)

computational_metagenomics_researcher.expert_description: Trained at the intersection of computer science and microbial ecology, this researcher specializes in machine learning-based metagenomic profiling, with deep experience in high-dimensional feature extraction from shotgun sequencing data. Their work centers on developing and applying supervised classification algorithms to taxonomic and functional gene abundance tables, transforming raw metagenomic reads into informative feature vectors that capture subtle compositional shifts. Typical research problems include biomarker discovery from complex microbial communities, cross-study validation of predictive models, and the computational deconvolution of strain-level functional potential. Core concepts woven into their daily practice involve random forests, gradient boosting, deep learning architectures for count data, metagenome-wide association frameworks, and functional annotation pipelines such as KEGG and eggNOG-mapper.

gastrointestinal_motility_physiologist.expert_description: Trained in clinical gastroenterology and gastrointestinal physiology, this researcher specializes in the objective quantification of human gut motor function. Their core methodological expertise lies in the application and interpretation of scintigraphic transit studies and wireless motility capsule (WMC) technology to measure regional and whole-gut transit times. Typical investigations focus on characterizing colonic transit profiles, including segmental retention patterns, as physiological discriminators of normal and disordered motility. Their work relies on empirical, non-invasive measurement of luminal content movement, generating high-fidelity spatiotemporal data on gastric emptying, small bowel transit, and colonic residence. Key concepts in their research include colonic geometric centers, pressure-derived motility indices, and the relationship between transit kinetics and luminal flow dynamics, informing a mechanistic understanding of functional bowel physiology.

systems_biology_modeler.expert_description: Trained in theoretical systems biology and metabolic network reconstruction, my research develops and applies constraint-based modeling frameworks to map the complex biochemical interactions between microbial communities and their hosts. I specialize in constructing genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) to simulate how microbial metabolic fluxes—particularly those governing the production of short-chain fatty acids—integrate with host metabolic and signaling networks. Typical problems in my group involve integrating multi-omics data to refine in silico representations of host-microbe metabolic exchange, analyzing pathway connectivity, and predicting how perturbations in microbial metabolism propagate to influence host cell functions. Core concepts and keywords in our work include flux balance analysis (FBA), community metabolic modeling, metabolite exchange networks, host-microbiome interactome inference, and the application of thermodynamic constraints to cross-species metabolic pathways.

translational_gastroenterology_clinical_.expert_description: A clinical researcher trained in gastroenterology with a dedicated focus on patient-centered phenotyping of chronic abdominal pain. Core expertise lies in the design, validation, and application of patient-reported outcome measures and quantitative sensory testing protocols to characterize visceral hypersensitivity in functional gastrointestinal disorders. Typical research involves developing standardized clinical tools to assess abdominal pain intensity, quality, and sensory thresholds, enabling stratification of patients by distinct pain phenotypes. Methodological approaches include psychophysical testing with barostat and thermal stimulation, psychometric validation of symptom diaries and questionnaires, and correlation of these clinical endpoints with underlying physiological mechanisms. Key concepts include visceral perception, allodynia, hyperalgesia, pressure-controlled distension, and the Rome diagnostic criteria, all aimed at bridging objective sensory assessment with the subjective patient experience.

microbial_metabolomics_biochemist.expert_description: Trained at the intersection of analytical chemistry and microbial ecology, I have spent over fifteen years applying high-resolution mass spectrometry to dissect the chemical dialogue within the gut ecosystem. My laboratory specializes in the targeted and untargeted metabolomics of bile acid profiles, using liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) and gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC-MS) to quantify primary and secondary bile acids and discover novel microbially conjugated forms. We focus on characterizing microbial bile acid modifications—including deconjugation, 7α-dehydroxylation, oxidation, and epimerization—to map specific biotransformation patterns onto the functional capacity of complex microbial communities. Our analytical pipelines integrate stable isotope tracing, enzymatic activity assays, and spectral networking to link molecular structures to the microbial taxa and genes responsible for their production. Core concepts guiding my work include bile salt hydrolase (BSH) activity, hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase (HSDH) pathways, enterohepatic circulation dynamics, and the use of metabolome-wide association studies to connect chemical phenotypes with ecological and physiological outcomes.

structure.problem_summary: This research topic investigates whether distinct gut microbiota profiles can differentiate irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C) from functional constipation (FC), two disorders sharing constipation symptoms but differing in underlying pathophysiology.
